Round one is approved. Here is round two, covering errors, edge cases, tests, and documentation impact.

**Errors.** The existing resolver in `settings/resolver.ts:12` validates the report-view setting. An invalid value falls back to the existing default, so no new error path, exception, or user-visible error state is added. The resolver handles a missing value the same way: `ui/report-view.ts:30` always receives a resolved value and never a raw or undefined one. The view adds no validation of its own, so every validity rule has one owner.

**Edge cases.**
- **Workspace change:** report filters keep their current values when the workspace changes. Switching workspaces does not reset the view's resolved setting or its filters.
- **Restart:** settings stay in memory, so a process restart returns the setting to its default. Persistence across restarts is out of scope.
- **Repeated workspace switches:** filters keep their values across multiple consecutive switches, not just the first one.
- **Default path:** when nobody sets the setting, the view behaves exactly as it does today.
- **Public surface:** the public API and config shape do not change. The setting stays private and is never exposed through any external surface.

**Tests.** Each line names an observable and its proposed test location. The file names follow the module paths; I'll confirm them against the repo's existing test layout when writing the spec.
- The resolver supplies the report-view default when no value is set - `settings/resolver.test.ts`
- The resolver returns the existing default for an invalid value - `settings/resolver.test.ts`
- The report view reads the resolved setting rather than a view-local settings object - `ui/report-view.test.ts`
- Report filters keep their values across a workspace change - `ui/report-view.test.ts`
- Filters keep their values across repeated workspace switches - `ui/report-view.test.ts`
- The setting returns to its default after a restart - none: settings live only in memory, so the reset is the absence of persistence, and no test can observe more than the default case above
- The public API and config shape are unchanged - none: the design adds no public surface, so nothing new exists to assert; existing public-contract tests cover regressions

**Documentation impact.** This section applies `reference/documentation-impact.md`. The gather draft lists `Docs touched: none`, so there are no amendment candidates to weigh. The setting is private and does not change any public API, config shape, or cross-component contract. No user guide covers this report view. Its default and fallback behavior are fully answered by the resolver code and its tests, so the setting does not qualify as a documented tunable parameter. No router, topic guide, or index becomes stale.

```markdown
- Derived / memory docs invalidated: none
```

The setting will use the existing resolver’s validation and fallback behavior. An invalid value resolves to the existing default; the report view will not introduce a separate fallback policy or duplicate the resolver’s defaults. `ui/report-view.ts:30` continues to consume resolved settings rather than interpreting raw values itself.

Settings remain in memory. This change adds no persistence mechanism and makes no promise that values survive an application restart. Workspace changes must preserve the current report-filter values, as approved in round one; switching workspaces must not reset those filters as a side effect of resolving or consuming the new setting.

The implementation remains private: there is no public API or configuration-shape change. Verification will therefore cover both the new setting’s behavior and regression protection for existing settings consumers. The tests should exercise the shared path, not a view-local substitute that could pass while bypassing the actual resolver.

- An invalid report-view setting falls back to that same default — resolver invalid-value test.
- A valid report-view setting reaches the view through the existing resolved-settings flow — report-view integration test.
- Current report-filter values remain unchanged after switching workspaces — workspace-switch regression test.
- Updating the setting uses in-memory state without introducing persistence — settings lifecycle test.
- Existing settings consumers retain their current resolution behavior — shared-resolver regression tests.
- Public API and configuration shapes remain unchanged — existing contract checks and diff review.

- Materially amended existing docs: none
